blocks.summary: High-yield rapid revision matrix targeting constitutional articles, non-statutory bodies, emergency provisions, and parliamentary committee traps.

blocks.content: 1. Constitutional Bodies (Article Mentioned): ECI (Art 324) | UPSC (Art 315) | CAG (Art 148) | Finance Commission (Art 280) | NCSC (Art 338) | NCST (Art 338A) | NCBC (Art 338B) | Attorney General (Art 76).
2. Non-Constitutional / Statutory Bodies: NHRC (Protection of Human Rights Act 1993) | CIC (RTI Act 2005) | CVC (CVC Act 2003) | NITI Aayog (Executive Resolution) | Lokpal (Lokpal Act 2013).
3. Parliamentary Committees: Public Accounts Committee (PAC - 22 members [15 LS + 7 RS], Chaired by Opposition) | Estimates Committee (**30 members - ALL from Lok Sabha!**).
4. 5 Prerogative Writs (Art 32 / 226): Habeas Corpus | Mandamus | Prohibition | Certiorari | Quo-Warranto.

blocks.text:
⚡ 1. Constitutional vs. Statutory Bodies Flash Table
| Body Name | Category | Creation Source / Article | Removal Authority & Process |
|---|---|---|---|
| **CAG of India** | Constitutional | **Article 148** | Same manner and grounds as Supreme Court Judge (Parliamentary address) |
| **Finance Commission** | Constitutional | **Article 280** | Constituted by President every 5 years |
| **Attorney General** | Constitutional | **Article 76** | Holds office during **pleasure of the President** (No fixed tenure) |
| **National Human Rights Comm (NHRC)**| **Statutory** | Protection of Human Rights Act 1993 | President (on SC inquiry report for misbehavior) |
| **Central Vigilance Comm (CVC)** | **Statutory** | CVC Act 2003 | President (on SC inquiry report) |
| **NITI Aayog** | **Executive Body**| Cabinet Resolution (Jan 1, 2015) | Executive discretion |

📖 2. Three Emergency Provisions Comparison Matrix
| Feature | National Emergency (Art 352) | President's Rule (Art 356) | Financial Emergency (Art 360) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Grounds** | War, External Aggression, Armed Rebellion | Failure of constitutional machinery in State | Threat to financial stability / credit of India |
| **Parliament Approval** | **1 Month** (Special Majority) | **2 Months** (Simple Majority) | **2 Months** (Simple Majority) |
| **Max Tenure** | Indefinite (renewed 6-monthly) | **Max 3 Years** (renewed 6-monthly) | Indefinite (No max limit; no re-approval needed!) |
| **FR Suspension** | Art 19 suspended (Art 358); Art 20 & 21 **NEVER suspended** | Fundamental Rights NOT affected | Fundamental Rights NOT affected |

⚖️ 3. Common Prelims & Mains Traps
- ⚠️ **Exam Trap 1:** The **Estimates Committee** consists of 30 members, and **ALL 30 members are drawn exclusively from LOK SABHA** (Rajya Sabha has zero representation!).
- ⚠️ **Exam Trap 2:** **Articles 20 and 21** can NEVER be suspended during any Emergency (44th Amendment Act 1978).

blocks.content:
#### Tier 1 — Recall MCQ
**Q:** Which of the following Parliamentary Standing Committees consists of 30 members drawn EXCLUSIVELY from the Lok Sabha, with zero representation from the Rajya Sabha?  
(A) Public Accounts Committee (PAC)  
(B) Estimates Committee  
(C) Committee on Public Undertakings (COPU)  
(D) Business Advisory Committee  
**Answer: — Estimates Committee has 30 members, all from Lok Sabha.

#### Tier 2 — Applied Scenario
**Scenario:** President proclaims a Financial Emergency under Article 360. Within what timeframe must Parliament approve it, and what is its maximum legal duration?  
**Resolution:** Must be approved within **2 months** by simple majority. Once approved, it continues **indefinitely** without needing periodic parliamentary re-approval.

#### Tier 3 — Mains Descriptive Prompt
*'Distinguish between Constitutional Bodies, Statutory Bodies, and Executive Bodies in India. How does the 44th Constitutional Amendment protect Articles 20 and 21 during National Emergency?'*
